B: Hello. I'm Riya.
A: Hello. Ioana.
B: Where are you?
A: Burnt Oak. North-west London. You?
B: Canada Water. Other side of the river, practically another country.
A: Yes. I don't go south very much. Only Tate.
B: I noticed the Hammershøi postcard on your fridge. In your photo.
A: Oh. Yes. You know him?
B: I was in Copenhagen last year. I saw a room of them at the SMK, the national gallery. I didn't expect to like them as much as I did. They're so empty, but they don't feel empty.
A: Yes, this is exactly it. There is always a door open, or a woman with her back. You want to know what she is thinking but he doesn't tell you. I saw some at National Gallery and I went back three times.
B: Three times to the same exhibition?
A: It was free, the room. I go in the mornings, I work evenings. So I have time.
B: What do you do?
A: Cleaner. At a primary school.
B: I go on weekday evenings, the Barbican mostly, or Tate Modern late opening. Fewer people talking loudly about brunch in front of the paintings.
A: Yes. Or taking photo of everything and not looking.
B: Exactly. I always go alone. People find that odd.
A: Me also. My husband comes once, he is finished after one hour, he wants coffee. I need maybe four.
B: What do you read? You had library books in the photo too.
A: Many things. Russian novels, Tolstoy, Chekhov stories. Ishiguro now, The Remains of the Day. Also I read in Romanian and French. I started literature at university in Iași, but I didn't finish. Money.
B: That's a shame. Do you read the Russians in French or English?
A: Romanian, usually. Sometimes French. The English ones I find in charity shop, fifty pence.
B: Then you've read more of them than most people who talk about them. I read mainly translated fiction. I'm halfway through a Korean novel. I keep a ranked list, which my friends think is excessive.
A: Ranked? Like a football table?
B: More or less. Ishiguro is high. Not that one, though. Never Let Me Go is better, I think. Remains of the Day is very controlled, but sometimes too controlled.
A: Hmm. I think the control is the point. He is a man who cannot let himself feel. So the book also does not let you. It is sad because it is so polite.
B: That's a good argument. I might have to move it up.
A: You can tell me what is at the top. I need new books.
B: Han Kang, probably. Human Acts. It's about Gwangju, the massacre. It's very hard to read but it's extraordinary. I recommended The Vegetarian to someone earlier, but for you I'd say Human Acts.
A: I will look in Hendon library. They are good, they order things.
B: Libraries are underrated. I mostly use a Kindle, which I'm aware is less romantic.
A: It is lighter on the bus. My bag is always too heavy, books and my lunch. And the 113 is always late, so I read standing at the stop.
